extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and commenters on the DHS public charge proposed rule; immigration practitioners, sureties, and federal agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of regulatory standards and procedural criteria from DHS's proposed public charge rule (Federal Register NPRM), to inform compliance, agency analysis, and notice-and-comment submissions. Covers federalism, NEPA, PRA, family assessment, bond rules, and other statutory/regulatory tests applied in the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: UMRA federal mandate determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule does not contain a Federal mandate as the term is defined under UMRA as it does not impose any enforceable duty upon any other level of government or private sector entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any downstream effects on State, local, or private entities would arise solely due to their voluntary choices and would not be a consequence of an enforceable duty imposed by this rule. Therefore title II of UMRA does not apply and DHS has not prepared a statement under UMRA. DHS has, however, analyzed potential effects in the Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) and welcomes comments on that analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would not have substantial direct effects on the States, on the relationship between the National Government and the States, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities among the various levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under section 6 of E.O. 13132, if the rule would have substantial direct effects on States or the Federal-State relationship or distribution of power, the agency must prepare a federalism summary impact statement. DHS determines this proposed rule lacks sufficient federalism implications to warrant that statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule was drafted and reviewed in accordance with E.O. 12988, Civil Justice Reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule should provide a clear legal standard for affected conduct, be reviewed to eliminate drafting errors and ambiguities, and minimize litigation and undue burden on the Federal court system. DHS has determined this rule meets the applicable standards in section 3 of E.O. 12988.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Policymaking Assessment criteria (Sec. 654)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must assess whether the regulatory action: (1) impacts the stability or safety of the family, particularly in terms of marital commitment; (2) impacts the authority of parents in the education, nurture, and supervision of their children; (3) helps the family perform its functions; (4) affects disposable income or poverty of families and children; (5) if the regulatory action financially impacts families, are justified; (6) may be carried out by State or local government or by the family; and (7) establishes a policy concerning the relationship between the behavior and personal responsibility of youth and the norms of society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the determination is affirmative for any of these points, the Agency must prepare an impact assessment addressing criteria specified in the law. DHS here determined the rule may decrease disposable income and increase poverty for certain families and children but concluded the benefits justify the financial impact and no further action is required. DHS also determined no impact on autonomy or integrity of the family as an institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 (Tribal consultation) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: This interim final rule would not have Tribal implications under E.O. 13175 because it would not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian Tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian Tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian Tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule would have substantial direct effects on Tribes or the Federal-Tribal relationship or distribution of power, tribal consultation and coordination requirements under E.O. 13175 would apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under DHS NEPA implementing procedures, for an action to be categorically excluded, it must satisfy each of the following three conditions: (1) the entire action clearly fits within one or more of the categorical exclusions; (2) the action is not a piece of a larger action; and (3) no extraordinary circumstances exist that create the potential for a significant environmental effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEPA allows agencies to list categorical exclusions for actions that do not have significant environmental effects. DHS's Instruction Manual Appendix A lists DHS Categorical Exclusions. DHS concluded this proposed rule amending regulations is strictly administrative/procedural, fits categorical exclusion A3, is not part of a larger Federal action, and does not present extraordinary circumstances creating potential for significant environmental effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paperwork Reduction Act, DHS must submit to OMB for review and approval any reporting requirements inherent in a rule, unless they are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information collection notice is published in the Federal Register to obtain comments regarding proposed edits to the information collection instrument. Comments are accepted for 60 days and must include the OMB Control Number in submissions. To avoid duplicate submissions, use only one of the methods under ADDRESSES. DHS and USCIS invite comments from the general public and other federal agencies on the impact to proposed collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA public comment points for information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on information collections should address one or more of the following four points: (1) Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility; (2) Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (3) Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (4) Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology, e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments addressing these points help OMB and the agency evaluate necessity, burden estimates, clarity, and burden-minimization. DHS provides 60-day comment windows and requires OMB Control Numbers to be included in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content for PRA information-collection notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Information-collection notices should include: (1) Type of Information Collection; (2) Title of the Form/Collection; (3) Agency form number and applicable DHS component; (4) Affected public and brief abstract of use; (5) An estimate of total number of respondents and estimated hour burden per response; (6) An estimate of total public burden (in hours) associated with the collection; and (7) An estimate of the total public burden (in cost) associated with the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS lists specific collections as examples (e.g., I-485 and supplements, I-945 Public Charge Bond, I-356 Request for Cancellation of a Public Charge Bond) and provides numeric burden estimates (respondents, hours per response, total annual hours and cost). These fields must be provided in PRA notices to enable commenter evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond cancellation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A public charge bond may be cancelled after the proper filing of a request for cancellation of a public charge bond on a form designated by USCIS for that purpose. The public charge bond will remain in effect until the form is filed and USCIS reviews the evidence and renders a decision regarding breach or cancellation. Bases for cancellation include: (i) the alien dies, departs permanently from the United States, or is naturalized, provided the alien did not breach the bond; (ii) substitution of another bond; (iii) USCIS cancellation upon review following the fifth anniversary of admission or adjustment if the alien has filed a request, has complied with all conditions on the bond, and USCIS finds no breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation requires submission of the designated form and USCIS review. The bond remains effective until USCIS renders a decision. The five-year automatic-consideration rule is conditioned on filing, compliance, and USCIS finding no breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond breach definitions and appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: A public charge bond submitted on or after [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF FINAL RULE PUBLICATION IN THE Federal Register] is breached if the bonded alien receives any means-tested public benefit prior to death, permanent departure, or naturalization, or is otherwise noncompliant with any conditions of the public charge bond. A public charge bond submitted before [DATE 60 DAYS AFTER DATE OF FINAL RULE PUBLICATION IN THE Federal Register] is breached if the bonded alien receives public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at Government expense, or is otherwise noncompliant with any condition of the public charge bond. A final public charge bond breach determination may be appealed by a surety under paragraph (f) of this section or by an alien under § 103.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule distinguishes breach standards by bond-submission date (post-rule effective date vs. pre-effective-date bonds). 'Means-tested public benefit' is defined as a trigger for breach after the new date, whereas pre-existing bonds use narrower triggers (public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization). Appeal routes for sureties and aliens are specified in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and nature of regulatory amendment (administrative/procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule is limited to removing existing regulatory criteria pertaining to public charge inadmissibility determinations and is strictly administrative and procedural; it would amend DHS's existing regulations to remove most of the provisions put into place by the 2022 Final Rule, however DHS officers would continue to make public charge inadmissibility determinations governed by existing law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS frames the action as an administrative change (not changing the underlying law or how officers exercise statutory discretion) and uses that framing to support categorical exclusion under NEPA and to limit other analyses. The NPRM also proposes removal of specific regulatory sections (e.g., removal of §§ 212.20 through 212.23).
